_comment: Copy to config/checks.json, which is git-ignored. The list of estate hostnames to probe is NOT here — it is derived from data/servers.json, so a site deployed today is checked today. This file holds only what cannot be derived: where to send the report, pages the estate does not host, and which forms may be submitted.

webhookHeaders._comment: Optional. If the n8n webhook uses header auth, put it here. This file is git-ignored, so a token is safe — but it never reaches data/ or the dashboard.

_notify_todo: Proving it end to end first, so only one inbox gets the noise. Add mdo60@kwgroup.in and mm3@kwgroup.in to `notify` once a real report has arrived.
_schedule_comment: One digest a day at reportAt, in `timezone` — NOT the server's clock. srv1340120 runs Etc/UTC, so a bare 09:30 would mail at 15:00 in Delhi. The probes run five times daily; nobody wants five identical 'all healthy' mails, which is how a report becomes a filter rule. The exception is alertOnNewFailures: something that breaks at 11:00 should not wait until tomorrow morning. Set it false if the morning mail is genuinely enough. npm run check -- --force-report mails now regardless.
_okStatus_comment: Not everything behind a hostname is a website. An MCP server has no route at "/", so a bare GET is a correct 404 — the endpoint is healthy and the question was wrong. List the statuses that mean alive for those. 502 and a refused connection still fail, because those mean the thing behind nginx is genuinely gone.
_extra_comment: Pages the estate does not serve, so nothing can discover them. The ad landing pages live on domains none of the three boxes has heard of — and they are where the leads come from, which makes them the pages that most need watching. Labelled by host + path so a failure names the page, not just the domain.
_forms_comment: A form is submitted ONLY if it appears here. Every run posts a real lead into a real CRM, so each entry is a deliberate decision. All sixteen landing pages post to the same submit.php per domain, so two entries cover them — probing all sixteen pages above is what catches an individual page being down. `fields` maps the page's real field names to the placeholders name/email/phone/message; any other value is sent literally. `expect` is a string the response must contain, because a submit.php that returns 200 and drops the lead is exactly the failure worth catching. Keep utm_source identical across forms — it is the single rule that filters every test lead out of the pipeline — and make utm_campaign per-site, because Campaign Name is a column in the Cratio list and two identical values there mean you cannot tell which landing domain the lead came from.

forms._verify_comment: No API key on disk. It asks n8n — which holds the Cratio API key as a Query Auth credential — over LOOPBACK, so the request never leaves the box and there is nothing here worth stealing. Import deploy/n8n-kw-lead-verify.json, attach a Query Auth credential named apikey, activate it. It searches Cratio by MOBILE rather than email: getRecordsBySearch uses @ as its field separator and the test email contains one, so an email search would never match. `match` is LEAD_FOUND rather than the email itself: a not-found reply that echoed the address back would read as a hit, which is the one failure mode that must never be silent. Delete this whole `verify` block to go back to 'the page accepted it'.
